races.title: State Senate, District 4
races.note: The top two finishers from the Nov 3, 2026 count. Everyone else in this race is coming.

cands.name: Buck Newton
cands.bio: Eldon Sharpe "Buck" Newton III is a Wilson attorney with a private practice, Newton and Lee. He served in the NC Senate for District 11 from 2011 to 2017 and has held District 4 since 2023. He was the 2016 Republican nominee for attorney general and once worked as an aide to Sen. Jesse Helms.
cands.gaps: We found no stated positions or actions from Newton on data centers, development and growth, homestead property taxes, out-of-state or investor land buying, immigration or H-1B. His campaign pages say nothing specific on these topics. Ballotpedia found no endorsements for him in 2026, and he did not complete Ballotpedia's candidate survey in 2022, 2024 or 2026. We did not have enough detail to describe his sponsored bills beyond the mask bill reported on Wikipedia. His campaign site is the only source for his stated positions, and the page was not clearly dated.

local.label: Roots 100: Ballotpedia and Wikipedia say he was born in Wilson, NC, and graduated from Hunt High School there, and he still lives in Wilson.

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: He served in the NC Senate from 2011 to 2017 and from 2023 on. He is a lawyer who has practiced for 16 to 20 years, owns a small business, formerly aided Sen. Jesse Helms on the U.S. Senate Foreign Relations Committee, and chaired the Wilson County Republican Party from 2007 to 2011.
qual.why: He has many years of prior legislative service plus a law career and small-business ownership, which fit the work of writing law and the state budget. Committee chairmanships were not counted.
qual.label: He has many years of prior legislative service plus a law career and small-business ownership, which fit the work of writing law and the state budget. Committee chairmanships were not counted.

pro-life.evidence: He says life begins at conception, calls himself 100% pro-life, and pledges to champion legislation to end abortion in North Carolina.

second-amendment.evidence: He says he will vigorously defend the 2nd Amendment and lists defending Second Amendment rights as a commitment.

back-police-order.evidence: His campaign site lists supporting law enforcement against radical defunding efforts as a commitment and describes his 2016 attorney general run as a law-and-order platform.

school-choice-teachers.evidence: His campaign site says he supported expanding school choice and five consecutive years of teacher pay raises.

prio.label: Matches 4 of 4 priorities; 0 backed by their record, 4 only promised

roots.summary: Ballotpedia and Wikipedia say he was born in Wilson, NC, and graduated from Hunt High School there, and he still lives in Wilson.

cands.name: Jessica (Jess) Rivera
cands.bio: Marine Corps veteran (2004–2012), barber and owner of The Garrison Barber & Parlor in downtown Wilson, NC. Democrat who won North Carolina State Senate District 4 (Greene, Wayne and Wilson Counties) in 2026, defeating incumbent Eldon Newton. She has held no prior elected office.

endorsements.text: In her Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey she lists endorsements from Run For Something, Victory LGBT, Vote Vets and Veterans For Responsible Leadership. She wrote that more would be added as applications were approved.
Ballotpedia lists Run for Something and several Sway voter-guide groups as recommending her, including NC Public School Champions and Fair Map Fight Club.

cands.gaps: We could not find her birthplace, where she was raised, or when she moved to North Carolina. Her campaign site says she "came home" to eastern North Carolina after COVID, but does not say what that means. She went to high school in Murrieta, California, but no page says where she grew up. We found no record of prior elected office, legislative work or policy staff work. We found no stated positions on homestead property taxes, foreign or institutional land buying, development and growth limits, immigration or H-1B, policing, gun laws, abortion, or school vouchers and charters. We found no documented controversies, foreign ties or notable endorsements beyond those listed. Her data-center stance is a platform statement with no bill or action behind it.

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: Served in the U.S. Marine Corps 2004–2012, including two Iraq tours. Licensed in cosmetology in 2017. Owns and runs The Garrison Barber & Parlor in Wilson, where she says she runs payroll. No prior legislative, policy or budget role found.
qual.why: Small-business ownership and management fall in the middle band. There is no legislative, policy or government budget experience on record, so she scores no higher.
qual.label: Small-business ownership and management fall in the middle band. There is no legislative, policy or government budget experience on record, so she scores no higher.

stop-data-centers.evidence: Her campaign platform has a section titled "Data Centers & Mandatory Moratoriums." It says: "We need a stronghold against the predatory nature of today's data centers. I will not allow our people to be poisoned for industry profits." It also says the district will hold companies to rigorous standards. The page gives no bill text or details.

school-choice-teachers.evidence: Her platform says she fights for well-funded rural schools and well-paid teachers. It names no raise percentage and takes no stated position on vouchers, charters or school choice.

prio.label: Matches 2 of 2 priorities; 0 backed by their record, 2 only promised
